input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 remediation of KServe serving images

## Description

Makes the KServe component images of the model serving stack compliant for
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters: no non-validated cryptographic modules in the
request path, and correct runtime behavior on FIPS-enabled clusters. The epic
also delivers the CI enforcement slice for KServe builds so that FIPS
regressions are caught at build time rather than rediscovered at certification.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe component images for cryptographic module usage, producing a
  per-image module inventory that identifies every non-validated crypto library
  linked in the request path
- Replace the non-validated crypto usage with validated cryptographic modules
  and rebuild the affected images
- Verify that the rebuilt images behave correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  clusters (the inference request path works end to end under FIPS-enabled
  crypto policy)
- Deliver and verify the FIPS regression gating check for KServe builds: a
  gating CI check that fails any KServe build that reintroduces non-validated
  crypto usage

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists for every KServe component image, enumerating the
  cryptographic modules linked in the request path and flagging non-validated
  usage
- No KServe component image links a non-validated cryptographic module in the
  request path, as verified by the module inventory and the gating check run
  against the final builds
- The rebuilt KServe images pass functional verification of the inference
  request path on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster
- A gating CI check runs on KServe builds and fails any build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (demonstrated by failing a
  deliberately non-compliant build)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): KServe portion of "all serving-stack images run correctly on
  FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules".
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the FIPS regression gating check for KServe builds is
  delivered and verified in this epic. Bundling rationale: the check shares the
  same images, builds, and CI configuration surface as the P0 remediation —
  the epic that converts a surface also authors and verifies enforcement for
  that surface. It is not independently deferrable: a standalone CI epic would
  build enforcement for surfaces this epic is still converting, leave this
  epic's enforcement slice incomplete, and force a second pass over the same
  build configuration.

# FIPS 140-3 remediation of Platform Operator and serving data plane images

## Description

Makes the Platform Operator component and the serving data plane images it
ships compliant for FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters: no non-validated
cryptographic modules in the request path, and correct runtime behavior on
FIPS-enabled clusters. The epic also delivers the CI enforcement slice for
these builds so that FIPS regressions are caught at build time rather than
rediscovered at certification.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator and serving data plane images for cryptographic
  module usage, producing a per-image module inventory that identifies every
  non-validated crypto library linked in the request path
- Replace the non-validated crypto usage with validated cryptographic modules
  and rebuild the affected images
- Verify that the rebuilt images behave correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  clusters (the serving data plane request path works end to end under
  FIPS-enabled crypto policy)
- Deliver and verify the FIPS regression gating check for these builds: a
  gating CI check that fails any Platform Operator or serving data plane build
  that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists for every Platform Operator and serving data plane
  image, enumerating the cryptographic modules linked in the request path and
  flagging non-validated usage
- No Platform Operator or serving data plane image links a non-validated
  cryptographic module in the request path, as verified by the module
  inventory and the gating check run against the final builds
- The rebuilt images pass functional verification of the serving request path
  on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster
- A gating CI check runs on these builds and fails any build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (demonstrated by failing a
  deliberately non-compliant build)

## Risks / Notes

- "Serving data plane" is scoped here to the images the strategy attributes to
  the Platform Operator component. If serving runtime images are intended,
  scope needs adjustment — flagged in the decomposition summary for PM
  confirmation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Platform Operator and serving data plane portion of "all
  serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated
  crypto modules".
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the FIPS regression gating check for these builds is
  delivered and verified in this epic. Bundling rationale: the check shares the
  same images, builds, and CI configuration surface as the P0 remediation —
  the epic that converts a surface also authors and verifies enforcement for
  that surface. It is not independently deferrable: a standalone CI epic would
  build enforcement for surfaces this epic is still converting, leave this
  epic's enforcement slice incomplete, and force a second pass over the same
  build configuration.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving
stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results for every
serving-stack image — and shepherds it through the mandatory security review
board sign-off milestones to submission at the external accredited
certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Establish the evidence package structure required by the security review
  board and the certification process
- Collect the per-image module inventories, build attestations, and
  FIPS-enabled-cluster test results produced by the serving-stack FIPS
  remediation work
- Assemble the complete evidence package and drive it through each security
  review board sign-off milestone defined for the certification process
- Submit the completed evidence package to the external accredited
  certification laboratory and confirm it is triaged

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations, and
  FIPS-enabled-cluster test results for every serving-stack image
- The evidence package has passed each security review board sign-off
  milestone defined for the certification process
- The evidence package has been submitted to the external accredited
  certification laboratory and its triage is confirmed

## Risks / Notes

- Certification-lab turnaround is historically six to nine months, and
  review-board cadence is fixed by that board. Both are externally controlled
  and cannot be compressed by engineering effort; they are schedule risks on
  this epic, not conditions its deliverable produces. The acceptance criteria
  therefore stop at the engineering completion point the team controls —
  package assembled, board milestones passed, submission made and triaged.
  The certification outcome itself is outside this strategy's requirements.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

# FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites documentation

## Description

Documents the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster
prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, as new
product documentation topics published in the platform documentation set.

## Scope

- New documentation topic stating the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack: what is supported on FIPS-enabled clusters, and what remains
  out of scope per the strategy (FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and
  training is covered by separate strategies; Common Criteria certification is
  out of scope)
- New documentation topic stating the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled
  operation of the serving stack
- Technical review of the drafted content against the implemented FIPS
  remediation and evidence work so the documented posture matches shipped
  behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled
  operation of the serving stack
- The documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented
  FIPS remediation and evidence package, and its statements match the shipped
  posture

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites. Priority note: this epic's priority is P0 per the
  docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter `priority:
  Critical` → P0), not from HLR-4's P2 label.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013 (FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack)

Triage (Step 0): not below-threshold (two affected components — KServe and
Platform Operator — and the certification work stream carries mandatory human
review-board gates and an external accredited laboratory, so ≥67% High AI
implementability does not hold); not documentation-only (image and CI code
changes are required). Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS 140-3 remediation of KServe serving images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS 140-3 remediation of Platform Operator and serving data plane images | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P0 |

Note on E004's priority: HLR-4 is P2, but the docs-authoring priority exception
derives the epic's priority from the strategy frontmatter `priority: Critical`
→ P0. This is rule-driven, not a priority inversion.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe image FIPS remediation (P0)"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator / data plane FIPS remediation (P0)"]
    E003["E003 Compliance evidence package and submission (P0)"]
    E004["E004 FIPS posture documentation (P0, docs-authoring)"]
    E001 --> E003
    E002 --> E003
    E001 --> E004
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

Critical path: E001 → E003 → E004 (length 3).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 14 + Step 5 shared-surface division | Different components, different repos, no shared artifacts → parallel. The HLR-3 FIPS-regression CI deliverable applies across the same builds being remediated, so it is divided per surface rather than extracted into a standalone CI epic: each remediation epic delivers and verifies the gating check for its own component's builds. A standalone enforcement epic would carve one logical change into a work-type epic and leave each remediation epic's slice incomplete. |
| E001 → E003 | Rules 12/13 (producer → consumer) | The evidence package is assembled from the remediation epics' primary engineering deliverables — the per-image module inventory, the build attestations, and the FIPS-enabled-cluster test results — and documents the remediated state, so it cannot truthfully be assembled before remediation completes. This is not the Rule 13 configuration-reference carve-out (image digests or build-pipeline side-effect attestations filled in at execution time): the consumed items here are the producing epic's core deliverables, and the security review board signs off on remediation evidence at its milestones. |
| E002 → E003 | Rules 12/13 (producer → consumer) | Same rationale as E001 → E003, for the Platform Operator and serving data plane images. |
| E001 → E004, E002 → E004, E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring last) | The documentation epic is blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy: docs describe what was built, including the FIPS support posture that only exists once remediation and evidence work land. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001, E002 | Split by component per the epic boundary rules: E001 covers the KServe component images; E002 covers the Platform Operator and serving data plane images. Together they cover "all serving-stack images". |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 | Evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001 (bundled), E002 (bundled) | The gating CI check runs over the same images, builds, and CI configuration surface that the P0 remediation converts — a shared surface, not a deferrable feature. Per the shared-surface enforcement rule the deliverable is divided per surface: the epic that converts a surface also authors and verifies the FIPS regression gate for that surface, so each remediation epic's HLR Traceability lists HLR-3 as bundled. Not independently deferrable: a standalone CI epic would build enforcement for surfaces another epic is still converting, leave each remediation epic's slice incomplete, and force a second pass over the same build configuration. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | New documentation topics (FIPS support posture, cluster prerequisites) are substantive content authoring — a distinct work-product stream → separate docs-authoring epic per the work-product boundary rule. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no per-component change/owner detail, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no NFRs. Teams were assigned by inference: KServe → RHOAI Serving (from `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`, "Owning team: RHOAI Serving"); Platform Operator → RHOAI Platform; evidence package → RHOAI Serving (owning team of the primary serving component); documentation → RHOAI Documentation. Confirm all four with the PM before scheduling.
2. **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file.** Only KServe has a context file under `.context/architecture-context/`. The strategy's premise is that Platform Operator already ships serving-stack images (it links non-validated crypto "today"), so it was treated as an existing component rather than generating a repo-onboarding chain — onboarding a new midstream repo would contradict the strategy's own problem statement. Consequence: `architecture_claims` is scored 0 for E002 and the component's repo/image inventory should be verified with its owning team.
3. **"Serving data plane" scope ambiguity.** The strategy attributes the serving data plane to Platform Operator (the only two Affected Components are KServe and Platform Operator). If Serving Runtimes images (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit — KServe's model-execution dependencies per the architecture context) are actually meant, E002's scope needs adjustment or a separate strategy; they are not in the declared scope here.
4. **External schedule gates are risks, not ACs.** Certification-lab turnaround (historically six to nine months) and review-board cadence are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They are recorded as Risks/Notes on E003; E003's acceptance criteria stop at the engineering completion point the team controls — package assembled, board milestones passed, package submitted to the lab and triaged. Certification outcome itself is not an in-scope deliverable.
5. **HLR-3 (P1) is bundled into P0 epics.** Deliberate, per the shared-surface enforcement rule — see the HLR-3 matrix row for the full rationale.
6. **No Investigation epics.** The strategy states "None on scope" for open questions and contains no conditional ADRs, pending reviews, or risks table. The crypto-usage audit (which images link non-validated crypto libraries) does not change which epics exist or what they do — remediation proceeds the same way regardless, and a failed audit finding is fix-and-retry within the same epic — so it is captured as an acceptance criterion (the per-image module inventory) on E001 and E002 rather than a separate Investigation.
7. **E001 and E002 may exceed the ~2-week epic guideline; conditional re-split trigger.** Each is a single-logical-change mechanical sweep (audit → remediate → rebuild → verify → CI gate) over one component's image set: splitting the sweep would separate the audit findings from the remediation that consumes them and the CI gate from the builds it verifies, so they are deliberately kept whole. The strategy enumerates no image count or effort estimate, so duration is unverified. Re-split trigger: if the module-inventory audit identifies materially more affected images than the strategy implies (rule of thumb: more than ~10 affected images per component, or the audit alone exceeding one week), or if capacity constraints require independently schedulable units, split the affected epic along the enumerated image set (e.g., per repo or per image group), each successor epic carrying its own audit/remediation/CI-gate slice, with new epic IDs continuing the sequence and the summary DAG updated accordingly.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable. The only external dependency with uncertain timing is the
accredited certification laboratory, and HLR-2's deliverable ends at submission
through the security review board — the certification outcome sits outside the
HLRs. All in-scope work (remediation, CI enforcement, evidence assembly,
documentation) proceeds without tiering; the lab gate lies after the last
in-scope deliverable.
